<script type="text/javascript">
    $(document).ready(function () {
        var popupClosedByEscape = false;
        $("#dropdownButtonSearch").on('click',function (event) {
            console.log('pressed');
           
             var intrvl = setInterval(function () {
                 setFocusElements_SearchDesktop(document.querySelector('#ctrlHeader_ctlDLSMenu_headernavRightMenu_txtQuickSearch_desktop'), document.querySelector('#ctrlHeader_ctlDLSMenu_headernavRightMenu_albsearch_desktop'));
                 clearInterval(intrvl);
               
             }, 500);
            
        });
    });
    function setFocusElements_SearchDesktop(firstElement, lastElement) {
        firstElement.focus();
        firstElement.addEventListener("keydown", (evt) => {
            if (evt.key === "Escape") {
                console.log('Escape-hide modalpopup');
                //$("#dropdownButtonSearch").click();
                $("#dropdownSearch_deskTop").removeClass('block').addClass("hidden");
                $("#dropdownSearch_deskTop").attr("aria-hidden", "true");
                $("#dropdownButtonSearch").focus()
                popupClosedByEscape = true;
            }
            else if (evt.key === "Tab") {
                // Prevent the default browser tab behavior (which moves focus to the next/previous element)
                //evt.preventDefault(); 
                
                if (evt.shiftKey) {
                    // Code to execute for Shift + Tab (backward navigation/dedent)
                    console.log("Shift + Tab was pressed (backward)");
                    // Add your custom logic here (e.g., move focus to the previous item)

                    evt.preventDefault();

                    lastElement.focus();
                } else {
                    // Code to execute for Tab (forward navigation/indent)
                    console.log("firstelem - Tab was pressed (forward)");
                    // Add your custom logic here (e.g., move focus to the next item)
                }
            }
        });

        lastElement.addEventListener("keydown", (evt) => {
             if (evt.key === "Escape") {
                 console.log('Escape-hide modalpopup');
                 //$("#dropdownButtonSearch").click();
                $("#dropdownSearch_deskTop").removeClass('block').addClass("hidden");
                $("#dropdownSearch_deskTop").attr("aria-hidden", "true");
                $("#dropdownButtonSearch").focus()
                popupClosedByEscape = true;
             }
            else if (evt.key === "Tab") {
                // Prevent the default browser tab behavior (which moves focus to the next/previous element)
                evt.preventDefault(); 

                if (evt.shiftKey) {
                    // Code to execute for Shift + Tab (backward navigation/dedent)
                    console.log("Shift + Tab was pressed (backward)");
                    // Add your custom logic here (e.g., move focus to the previous item)

   
                } else {
                    // Code to execute for Tab (forward navigation/indent)
                    console.log("lastelem - Tab was pressed (forward)");
                    // Add your custom logic here (e.g., move focus to the next item)
                     firstElement.focus();
                }
            }
        });
    }
</script>

<script language="javascript" type="text/javascript">
    $(document).ready(function () {
        $(".submenu-btn").each(function () {
            $(this).on("click", function() {
                console.log('submenu clicked');
                var currentElemExpandState = $(this).parent().find('a:first').attr('aria-expanded');

                //reset all others
                $("li.menu-item-has-children > a ").attr('aria-expanded', 'false');

                if (currentElemExpandState == 'false') {
                    $(this).parent().find('a:first').attr('aria-expanded', 'true');
                }
                else {
                    $(this).parent().find('a:first').attr('aria-expanded', 'false');
                }
                
            });
        });
    });
</script>

<script>

    function readpagespeaker() {
        //console.log('readspeaker calling...');
         if ($('div#readspeaker_button1').hasClass('disable'))
         {         

            $('#readSpeakerBox').addClass('rsfloating').addClass('rsexpanded');

         else {
             $('div#readspeaker_button1').addClass('disable');
             $('div#readspeaker_button1 .rsbtn_stop').click();
            $('#readSpeakerBox').removeClass('rsfloating').removeClass('rsexpanded');

         }
        }

        function resetReader()
        {
            $('div#readspeaker_button1 a.rsbtn_stop').click(function () {
                 $('div#readspeaker_button1').addClass('disable');
                 $('div#readspeaker_button1 .rsbtn_stop').click();

    function highlightSearch_header() {
        //console.log($('input.advancedsearch_input_header').length);
        if ($('input.advancedsearch_input_header').length == 0)
            return;

        var keyword = $('input.advancedsearch_input_header').val();
        if (keyword.length > 0) {

            $('.highlight > .row').each(function (j) {
                //Title
                var higlightTitleContent = $(this).find('h2 a').html().replace(new RegExp(keyword, "ig"), "<highlight>" + keyword + "</highlight>");
                $(this).find('h2 a').html(higlightTitleContent);

                //Details
                var higlightDetailsContent = $(this).find('.newslistdescription').html().replace(new RegExp(keyword, "ig"), "<highlight>" + keyword + "</highlight>");
                $(this).find('.newslistdescription').html(higlightDetailsContent);
            });

        }
    }

    function highlightSearch_header_desktop() {
        //console.log($('input.advancedsearch_input_header').length);
        if ($('input.advancedsearch_input_header_desktop').length == 0)
            return;

        var keyword = $('input.advancedsearch_input_header_desktop').val();
        if (keyword.length > 0) {

            $('.highlight > .row').each(function (j) {
                //Title
                var higlightTitleContent = $(this).find('h2 a').html().replace(new RegExp(keyword, "ig"), "<highlight>" + keyword + "</highlight>");
                $(this).find('h2 a').html(higlightTitleContent);

                //Details
                var higlightDetailsContent = $(this).find('.newslistdescription').html().replace(new RegExp(keyword, "ig"), "<highlight>" + keyword + "</highlight>");
                $(this).find('.newslistdescription').html(higlightDetailsContent);
            });

        }
    }

    function callAddthisScript(id, as, src) {
        if (document.getElementById(id)) return;
        var hjs = document.getElementsByTagName('head')[0], js = document.createElement('script');
        js.id = id; js.type = 'text/javascript'; js.async = as; js.src = src;
        document.body.appendChild(js);
        //  hjs.appendChild(js);
    }

    function togglePersonalizeBar() {        
        $('div#divAccessibility').toggleClass('disable-wrapper', 1000);

        $('html, body').animate({
            scrollTop: $('div#divAccessibility').offset().top
        }, 800, function () {

            // Add hash (#) to URL when done scrolling (default click behavior)
            window.location.hash = "#divAccessibility";
        });
        hideToolTipBaloon();
    }

    function toggleFloatingSideBar() {
        $('div.sideFloatingMenu').slideToggle("slow");
        hideToolTipBaloon();
        
        //$('div.sideFloatingMenu').toggleClass('disable-wrapper', 1000);
        $('html, body').animate({
            scrollTop: 0
        }, 800, function () {
            // Add hash (#) to URL when done scrolling (default click behavior)
            window.location.hash = "#divAccessibility";
        });
    }

             <div id="ctrlContentArea_NewsList2013724114611_divFqsList" class="col-md-12" style="margin-top:1.5rem">
                  <h3 class="selecteCategory">Corporate TAX FAQs </h3>
            <!-- List Start -->
                
             
              <div id="accordion" class="faq-list highlight border-aeblack-100 aegov-accordion rounded-xl border !p-8 [&_.accordion-active_svg]:rotate-180">
                
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_0"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_0" aria-controls="collapseFaq_0"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>1. What is a “Business” or “Business Activity”?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_0" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_0" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            The terms “Business” and “Business Activity” as defined in the Corporate Tax Law identify when the activities of certain persons give rise to a UAE CT liability by considering the person to be a taxable person. <br />
<br />
“Business” means any economic activity, whether continuous or short term, conducted by any person. It is implied that a business is conducted with a profit motive, and that there is the existence of some system and organisation to the activity conducted. However, a business or business activity for UAE CT purposes does not lose its identity simply because it does not make a profit.<br />
<br />
For the application of the Corporate Tax Law to companies and other juridical persons, all activities conducted and assets used or held will generally be considered activities conducted, and assets used or held, for the purposes of a “Business”.<br />
<br />
Individuals can earn income from wages and salaries, investments or from practising a commercial, industrial or professional activity, either directly or as sole proprietor of a business. For natural persons, a Cabinet Decision will be issued in due course specifying further information on what would bring a natural person within the scope of UAE CT. <br />
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_1"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_1" aria-controls="collapseFaq_1"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>2. Will the income of UAE branches of a UAE business be subject to UAE CT?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_1" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_1" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            Yes. The income of UAE branches will be included in the taxable income and UAE CT return of their UAE “parent” or “head office”.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_2"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_2" aria-controls="collapseFaq_2"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>3. Will transfer pricing rules apply to both domestic and cross border transactions? </span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_2" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_2" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            Yes. Transfer pricing rules apply to UAE businesses that have transactions with Related Parties and Connected Persons, irrespective of whether the Related Parties or Connected Persons are located in the UAE mainland, a Free Zone or in a foreign jurisdiction.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_3"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_3" aria-controls="collapseFaq_3"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>4. I am already registered for VAT purposes. Do I have to register for UAE CT?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_3" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_3" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            Yes. Taxpayers will be required to register for UAE CT (and update their details, if required), even if they are already registered for VAT.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_4"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_4" aria-controls="collapseFaq_4"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>5. What is CT?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_4" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_4" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            CT is a form of direct tax levied on the net income or profit of corporations and other businesses. CT is sometimes also referred to as “Corporate Income Tax” or “Business Profits Tax” in other jurisdictions.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_5"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_5" aria-controls="collapseFaq_5"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>6. Will UAE branches of foreign businesses be subject to UAE CT?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_5" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_5" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            Where no election is made or the income of the foreign branch or permanent establishment is not eligible for an exemption from CT, the UAE CT payable on the income of the foreign branch or permanent establishment can be reduced by the corporate tax (or similar) paid on the relevant income in the foreign jurisdiction. 
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_6"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_6" aria-controls="collapseFaq_6"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>7. Why is the UAE introducing CT?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_6" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_6" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            A competitive CT regime based on international best practices is expected to cement the UAE’s position as a leading global hub for business and investment and accelerate the UAE’s development and transformation to achieve its strategic objectives.  <br />
<br />
Introducing a CT regime also reaffirms the UAE’s commitment to meeting international standards for tax transparency and preventing harmful tax practices.<br />
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_7"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_7" aria-controls="collapseFaq_7"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>8. Who is a Natural Person?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_7" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_7" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            The term “Natural Person” in the Corporate Tax Law means an individual.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_8"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_8" aria-controls="collapseFaq_8"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>9. Is the UAE the first country to introduce CT?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_8" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_8" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            Most countries in the world have a comprehensive CT regime, including most of the countries in the Middle East.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_9"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_9" aria-controls="collapseFaq_9"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>10. When will the UAE CT regime become effective?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_9" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_9" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            The UAE CT regime will become effective for financial years starting on or after 1 June 2023.<br />
<br />
Examples:<br />
●	A business that has a financial year starting on 1 July 2023 and ending on 30 June 2024 will become subject to UAE CT from 1 July 2023 (which is the beginning of the first financial year that starts on or after 1 June 2023)<br />
●	A business that has a financial year starting on 1 January 2023 and ending on 31 December 2023 will become subject to UAE CT from 1 January 2024 (which is the beginning of the first financial year that starts on or after 1 June 2023)<br />
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_10"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_10" aria-controls="collapseFaq_10"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>11. Are UAE branches separate juridical persons?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_10" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_10" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            No. UAE branches of a domestic or a foreign juridical person are an extension of their “parent” or “head office” and, therefore, are not considered separate juridical persons.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_11"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_11" aria-controls="collapseFaq_11"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>12. Who will be subject to UAE CT?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_11" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_11" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            UAE CT applies to juridical persons incorporated in the UAE and juridical persons effectively managed and controlled in the UAE, as well as to foreign juridical persons that have a permanent establishment (see section Foreign persons) in the UAE (see question ‘Who is considered resident for UAE CT purposes?’ under section Scope and rate).<br />
Individuals will be subject to CT only if they are engaged in a business or business activity in the UAE, either directly or through an unincorporated partnership or sole proprietorship. A Cabinet Decision will be issued in due course specifying further information on what would bring a natural person within the scope of UAE CT.      <br />
<div> </div>
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_12"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_12" aria-controls="collapseFaq_12"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>13. Will UAE entities owned by UAE or GCC nationals be subject to UAE CT?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_12" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_12" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            Yes – the UAE CT does not differentiate between nationality or residence. Juridical persons that are incorporated or resident in the UAE, or that have a permanent establishment in the UAE, will be subject to UAE CT. This applies irrespective of the residence and nationality of the individual founders or (ultimate) owners of the entity.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_13"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_13" aria-controls="collapseFaq_13"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>14. Will foreign companies and other juridical persons be subject to UAE CT?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_13" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_13" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            Foreign entities that operate in the UAE through a permanent establishment or that are considered resident in the UAE for CT purposes will be subject to UAE CT. Merely earning UAE sourced income would not trigger CT payable or require the foreign entity to register and file for UAE CT.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_14"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_14" aria-controls="collapseFaq_14"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>15. Will UAE CT be applicable to businesses in each Emirate?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_14" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_14" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            Yes. The UAE CT is a Federal tax and will therefore apply across all the Emirates.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_15"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_15" aria-controls="collapseFaq_15"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>16. Will I have to pay UAE CT alongside Emirate level taxes?  </span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_15" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_15" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            Businesses engaged in the extraction of the UAE’s natural resources and in certain non-extractive activities that are subject to Emirate level taxation will be outside the scope of UAE CT, subject to meeting certain conditions. Other businesses may be subject to both Federal CT and Emirate level taxation. Emirate level taxes paid will not be able to be credited against or otherwise reduce the amount of Federal CT payable.<br />
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_16"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_16" aria-controls="collapseFaq_16"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>17. What is taxable income?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_16" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_16" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            The taxable income for a Tax Period is the accounting net profit (or loss) of the business, after making adjustments for certain items as defined in the Corporate Tax Law. 
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_17"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_17" aria-controls="collapseFaq_17"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>18. Will UAE CT replace VAT in the UAE?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_17" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_17" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            No, CT and VAT are two different types of taxes. Both will continue to apply in the UAE.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_18"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_18" aria-controls="collapseFaq_18"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>19. What expenditure will be deductible for the purposes of calculating taxable income?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_18" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_18" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            In principle, all legitimate business expenses incurred to derive taxable income will be deductible, although the timing of the deduction may vary for different types of expenses and the accounting method applied. For capital assets, expenditure would generally be recognised by way of depreciation or amortisation deductions over the economic life of the asset or benefit.<br />
<br />
Expenditure that has a dual purpose, such as expenses incurred for both personal and business purposes, will need to be apportioned with the relevant portion of the expenditure treated as incurred wholly and exclusively for the purpose of the taxable person’s business.<br />
<div> </div>
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		
				 <div class="faq-item accordion-item">
                     <h6 class="faq-heading accordion-title" id="heading_19"> 
                         <button type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#collapseFaq_19" aria-controls="collapseFaq_19"  class="collapsed" aria-expanded="false">
				            <span>20. Will I have to pay UAE CT alongside VAT in the UAE?</span>
				            <span class="pull-right"><i class="ph-bold ph-plus"></i></span>
			            </button>
                           
                       
                     </h6>

                    <div  id="collapseFaq_19" class="faq-body accordion-content collapse" aria-labelledby="heading_19" data-bs-parent="#accordion">                                            
                            If you are a registered business for VAT, you will have to pay VAT and CT separately. If your business is not VAT registered you may still have to pay CT.
                            <div class="clear10"></div>                                                                             
                    </div>
                </div>
		 </div>

<script type="text/javascript">

    var slideShareCloser = null;
    function slideShare(obj) {
        clearTimeout(slideShareCloser);
        slideShareCloser = null;
        $(obj).parent().find('div.shareBox-hover').unbind('mouseleave');

        if ($(obj).parent().find('div.shareBox-hover').hasClass('showShareBox')) {
            $(obj).parent().find('div.shareBox-hover').removeClass('showShareBox');
        }
        else {
            $(obj).parent().find('div.shareBox-hover').addClass('showShareBox');
            setTimeout(function () {
                $(obj).parent().find('div.shareBox-hover').bind('mouseleave', function () {
                    slideShareCloser = setTimeout(function () { $(obj).parent().find('div.shareBox-hover').removeClass('showShareBox'); $(obj).parent().find('div.shareBox-hover').unbind('mouseleave'); }, 5000);
                });
            }, 250);
        }
    }


</script>
